subject: Extract parameters after running nimbleMCMC() function

messages.author: 8aa7b9e8ebc839ba
messages.subject: Extract parameters after running nimbleMCMC() function
parts:
Good afternoon,

Sorry because I think it is a simple question, but I do not manage to extract the parameters from a NIMBLE model using three chains and run with nimbleMCMC function. I have saved the output in a .RDS file, and my output's structure I is:

num [1:27000, 1:667] -1.96 -1.96 -1.96 -1.96 -1.96 ...
 - attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
  ..$ : NULL
  ..$ : chr [1:667] "alpha[1]" "alpha[2]" "alpha[3]" "alpha[4]" ...

Doing dimnames(output) I get all my paremeters' names, but I have time and age dependencies on them and also a larrge number of parameters and I am sure there should be a easy way to extract the values (I guess similar than it is done in JAGS). Any help would be appreciated.

Thanks in advance,

Blanca

messages.author: e294dd6d325c0bfa
messages.subject: Re: Extract parameters after running nimbleMCMC() function
parts:
Blanca 
 I have had exactly the same question - mostly around getting out specific parameters, because they are age or time dependent and I'm interested in specific ones. I wrote a couple of functions to do this, see below, that work for me. I don't guarantee they will do exactly what you want but hopefully they should point you in the right direction. If they do work I also have functions that quickly plot trace/density plots and the mean/cl estimates for different parameters of the same name (eg your alpha's) which I am happy to share directly. They should work with single or parallel output.
Hope that helps. If anyone would like to point out a better/more efficient way of doing this then please feel free :)
Have a good weekend all 
Cheers
Rob

###
get.parm <- function(x, parm=''){ # x is a nimble MCMC object, parm is a character string of the parameter name
 
  extract.cols <- function(x) as.data.frame(x[ , grep(parm, dimnames(x)[[2]], fixed=TRUE)])
  return(data.table::rbindlist(lapply(x, extract.cols)))

}

summarise <- function(x, parm){
 
  samples <- as.data.frame(get.parm(x, parm))
  cat(c("Par     Min    2.5%    25%   Median    Mean     75%    97.5%    Max\n"))
  for( i in 1:ncol(samples) ){
    cat(c(sprintf("%3i", i),
          sprintf("%7.3f", min(samples[ , i])),
          sprintf("%7.3f", quantile(samples[ , i],c(0.025, 0.25, 0.5))),
          sprintf("%7.3f", mean(samples[ , i])),
          sprintf("%7.3f", quantile(samples[ , i],c(0.75, 0.975))),
          sprintf("%7.3f", max(samples[ , i]))))
    cat('\n')
  }

}

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Extract parameters after running nimbleMCMC() function
parts:
Thanks for the question Blanca and for the good suggestion in response Rob.

Another way to work with samples that you may find helpful is to extract the samples as a list, with an element for each monitored variable. This will require that you take the steps of nimbleModel, buildMCMC, and compileMCMC yourself rather than relying on nimbleMCMC to do it.  Say that cMCMC is the compiled MCMC object.  After running it (possibly via runMCMC, or via cMCMC$run), you can do as.list(cMCMC$mvSamples) and you will get a list back rather than a matrix.  Unfortunately if you are using runMCMC for multiple chains, this will only extract the samples from the last chain.  There is no option for runMCMC to do it for each chain as it processes the results of each one. 

-Perry
